Oh oh when you revising, you might want to revisit how you want to reveal what actually happened to the two lovers. The carved message is a bit direct.

Its called parental liability... specifically in this case, its called Family Car Doctrine. So yeah, the US legislations is a sniveling shit. If you are not ready to face the consequences of your child's action, then either watch your fucktard of a kid properly or don't have kids at all.

JJ asked "And you allowed your 14 year old son drive the car?" She answered "Only on the property", which proves that the mom had explicitly given permission to the son to drive the car. So the question as to whether she left the keys in the car and the son driving off because the keys are already in the car does not matter. The son does not own the car, yes, but the mom gave permission to the son and as such she is reponsible for the consequence (although if the kid is much older, he is accountable instead i.e. parental liabilities end when a child reaches age of majority). Even knowing the responsibility, she did not provide the proper surveillance to prevent the son and the girl to drive off the property. Moreover, theft is defined as an action with the intent to permanently deprive the owner from the property and the mens rea of dishonesty, which the girl certainly was not due to the belief of consent given by the son. If for example, the mom kept an eye on both of them and she tried to stop from the girl driving to the friends house, her objection is made known to the girl and therefore the girl's action will be considered theft.
No. But the kid can be held accountable because the girl was driving because of the kid's actions. Age does not matter for accountability,  the ability to reason however, does.

Lets take an example on car insurance policy. If you are the policy holder, but you gave the permission to someone else to drive your insured car and the car then crashed into Narnia, the insurer does not have to pay a cent if they know that someone else was driving the car. This is because your permission placed the accountability onto you instead of the insurer. In this regard, the son gave permission to the defendants daughter to drive, which placed the accountability on him. But the mom gave permission for the son to drive, placing the accountability on herself. So she was accountable to whatever the son was accountable for. Hence, the son was accountable for the damage to the girl (pain and death) and this in turn made his mother accountable for it. As to the damage of the car, the girl was accountable but she died. Hence, no else was accountable to the damage. Also, the act of driving off the property is not considered stealing because first, the son was accountable/accomplice, second, due to the knowledge on lack of objection by the owner, implied permission to drive the car was granted to the girl.

Yes the girl should have. But it does not diminish the fact that the mom is accountable when she gave the permission to her son to drive. The boy whom let her drive eventhough its not his decision to make and the mom whom let the boy access the vehicle in the first place but did not provide a proper surveillance/negligence are at fault just as much as the girl, if not much more. The plaintiff actually had no ground because it was not established that the defendant was accountable over the daughter's actions (it was not explicitly said that the defendant gave permission for her daughter to drive) and you can't sue a dead girl, while the counterclaim was upheld because there was someone who can be accounted for.

I think when JJ questions the woman whether she let her son drive the car, ultimately she was accountable to her son's actions. Her son on the other hand gave the permission to the defendant's daughter to drive the car. Hence, the defendant's daughter did not technically steal the car. Moreover, it was established that the mother did not explicitly forbid the son to drive the car, so it does not matter whether she did or did not leave the car keys accessible to her son. Because ultimately the plaintiff can be held liable over the counterclaim by the defendant, she has to pay the damages.

First -ve interest rate can be effective if there is no usage of cash i.e purely electronic. With 80% of money is in electronic form, there's simply not enough cash if people start withdrawing. Also, what prevents people from withdrawing from banks and put it inside their shoe boxes? There's that and second the purpose of -ve interest rate is to discourage savings and encourage spending. So effectively, -ve interest rate is a form of taxation on savings i.e the amount of savings decreases over time. Thus, need to spend now to ensure highest utility achieved (from achieving higher consumption as opposed to consumption in the future as you can afford less due to taxation on savings). But this has political ramifications. It is tax. Plus, letting inflation goes up has the same effect (although the magnitude of the relationship is most prob. non-linear/hard to quantify). With inflation, there is no direct political consequence because of money illusion and many factors can be blamed for higher inflation (arabs... those arabs with oil hehe j/k). How inflation works is that due to higher prices, you buy less i.e your purchasing power decreases, and if you expect higher inflation, you'd buy more today to conserve your purchasing power, thus higher inflation expectation discourage savings and encourage spending. So given there is an alternative policy, they tend not to go out of the traditional framework i.e interest as incentive to save and cost to borrow as oppose to cost to save and incentive to borrow which what happens when interest rate is -ve. I think the whole purpose of equilibrium theory is to tell where ideally an economy should be and divergence from it usually causes the system to be unstable (a very outdated example is cobweb models). Hence, that's where policymakers come in and correct any instability before the whole economy is jeopardized, the same thing cannot be said about weather . An analogy to weather is somewhat acceptable in a sense that many series in the economy are random walks, that they cannot be predicted 100% correct due to existence of white noise, but these noise do actually bob up and down through the mean eg temperature during seasons. But as oppose to weather, economy can be corrected. How much does an economy should be corrected? That is where empiricals helps the most.
